\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শিম} (shim)}{শিম (shim)}]{\bn{শিম} (shim) — beans}

\label{lesson:BN-C117-shim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for ginger, then the Bengali for a tomato.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শিম}}
\textbf{\bn{শিম}} — \emph{shim} — \textquotedblleft{}beans\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শিম}} (\emph{shim}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{śimba}, \textquotedblleft{}pod, legume\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12445).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কুমড়ো} (kumṛo)}{কুমড়ো (kumṛo)}]{\bn{কুমড়ো} (kumṛo) — a pumpkin}

\label{lesson:BN-C117-kumro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a tomato, then the Bengali for beans.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কুমড়ো}}
\textbf{\bn{কুমড়ো}} — \emph{kumṛo} — \textquotedblleft{}a pumpkin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কুমড়ো}} (\emph{kumṛo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*kohaṇḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}pumpkin-gourd\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 3374). It stands beside Sanskrit \emph{kuṣmāṇḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}pumpkin-gourd\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL writes the Bengali forms \emph{kõrā} and \emph{kohõṛā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{চাল} (chāl)}{চাল (chāl)}]{\bn{চাল} (chāl) — uncooked rice}

\label{lesson:BN-C117-chal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for leafy greens, then the Bengali for a radish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{চাল}}
\textbf{\bn{চাল}} — \emph{chāl} — \textquotedblleft{}uncooked rice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{চাল}} (\emph{chāl}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*cāmala}, \textquotedblleft{}husked rice\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 4749). CDIAL thinks it possibly of the same non-Aryan origin as Sanskrit \emph{taṇḍula}, \textquotedblleft{}rice\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
